title: AI for Forecasting
summary: Rebuild your forecast in minutes, not a full afternoon.
description: Using AI inside Excel to speed up forecasting and budgeting cycles.
agenda: We'll use AI inside Excel to speed up your forecasting and budgeting cycles.
takeaways: A forecast rebuilt in minutes instead of an afternoon.
prerequisites: Excel experience, familiarity with your forecasting process

title: Red-Teaming Decisions with AI Agents
summary: Before you commit, let a panel of AI advisors try to talk you out of it.
description: Watch AI agents challenge a real business decision from every angle, then see how the panel is built.
agenda: A live decision gets challenged
takeaways: A repeatable way to pressure-test big decisions before you make them.

title: Automated Meeting Notes (Voice and Transcripts)
summary: See a meeting turn into clean notes, decisions and follow-ups with no typing.
description: A live demo takes a recorded meeting through to finished notes and a task list, and shows how to make them trustworthy.
agenda: A live demo from recording to finished notes, then what makes the notes trustworthy and how to roll it out to your team.
takeaways: A simple setup that ends manual note-taking and lost action ite

title: Task and Project Visibility
summary: Know where everything stands without chasing anyone.
description: See one live view of tasks and projects that AI keeps current from your email and meetings.
agenda: A live dashboard built from real-style activity, how it stays accurate, and what to track first.
takeaways: A plan for a status view that updates itself.

title: AI for Email Drafting
summary: Clear your inbox in your own voice, with you in control of what goes out.
description: Watch AI draft replies that sound like you, and see how every draft is reviewed by you before anything is sent.
agenda: Live drafting on real-style emails, how the AI learns your tone, and how drafts get reviewed before sending.
takeaways: A drafting routine that saves time without risking a bad send.

title: Orchestrating Agents for Daily Work
summary: See a team of AI agents run a piece of your day while you do something else.
description: An agent team handles a real workflow live, then we show how it is put together.
agenda: The orchestrator runs live, we explain how it works in plain language, and then pick the first workflow worth automating.
takeaways: A clear view of what agent teams can do for your business and where to start.

title: AI and Excel for Forecasting
summary: Build a forecast in an afternoon and know how far to trust it.
description: See how to use AI with Excel to build and stress-test a forecast.
agenda: A forecast built live, testing the assumptions, and presenting a range instead of a single number.
takeaways: A forecast method you can reuse and defend.

title: AI for Executive Reporting
summary: Turn raw financial data into board and leadership reports in minutes.
description: Watch AI turn raw numbers into a clear executive summary, and learn the review steps that keep it accurate.
agenda: A live data-to-report demo, how to keep the story accurate, and the review steps before it goes to the board.
takeaways: A template for a monthly report that takes minutes, not days.

title: Organizing Data for AI
summary: Learn how to organize your files and records so AI can find and use them.
description: We show a simple way to structure your folders, documents and data so AI gives you better answers without a big IT project.
agenda: A messy set of files organized live, the simple rules that make it work, and how to keep it organized.
takeaways: A simple filing structure you can apply to your own data this week.

title: Q1 2027 Cohort: AI for Business Executives,
summary: The first class of our Q1 2027 cohort, a live, hands-on program where non-coding executives learn to build AI agents for their own work.
description:
Our Q1 2027 cohort, AI for Business Executives, starts the week of January 11. It is a live, guided program for leaders who do not code but want AI to take real work off their plate.

Each week has one 90-minute live session: a short lesson, a live demo, then hands-on practice with help in the room. Weekly office hours give you time to bring questions and anything that did not work.

Early sessions cover getting set up, building a meeting and note-taker workflow, and an accounting workflow. Later sessions move into assistants and agents built for your own role.

Seats are limited to 30. Join the interest list to save your spot and get the full curriculum when it is released.
agenda: Welcome and how the cohort works
What AI agents are and what they can do for an executive
Getting set up: accounts and connecting email, calendar and files
Live demo: an assistant working on real tasks
Hands-on: set up your own workspace with help
Wrap-up and first homework
takeaways: A working AI setup connected to your email, calendar and files
A clear picture of what you will build over the cohort
Your first small task automated
A plan for which work to hand to AI first
prerequisites: No coding experience needed.

title: One Idea, Every Format: Production Without the Resizing
summary: Turn one approved idea into every platform format, with your words and images left exactly as you made them.
description: A single idea has to become a LinkedIn image, an Instagram post, a vertical cover and a short animation. This session shows how to do that without another round in a design tool for each one. Live: /wf-design places your exact copy and your own images into Canva layouts at each platform size and waits for your pick. /wf-motion turns the same message into a 6 to 10 second animation. Every output is checked before you see it, and you approve every result. Presented by James Christopher.
agenda: 1. One idea, every format: a LinkedIn image, an Instagram post, a vertical cover and a short animation
2. Live: /wf-design places your exact copy and your own images into Canva layouts at each platform size
3. Live: /wf-motion turns the same message into a 6 to 10 second animation
4. Check every output and approve every result
takeaways: A one-idea, every-format checklist
prerequisites: Attend Set Up Your Local Agentic System on Nov 20, or have Claude Code installed and working on your computer. Codex also works, but Claude Code is preferred.

title: Video Without the Editing Bay
summary: Get from one long recording to captioned shorts and a thumbnail, without days of editing.
description: One good recording can feed a month of posts, if someone has the hours to cut it. This session shows how to get from footage you already have to vertical shorts with captions, clean audio and a thumbnail. Live: /vid pulls shorts from a long video, and /wf-design youtube builds thumbnail layouts. Speaker quotes are used only when the speaker has approved them. You choose the moments. The tools do the cutting. Presented by James Christopher.
agenda: 1. From one long recording to vertical shorts with captions, clean audio and a thumbnail
2. Live: /vid pulls shorts from a long video
3. Live: /wf-design youtube builds thumbnail layouts
4. Choose the moments and check the cuts
takeaways: A one-recording, many-posts plan
prerequisites: Attend Set Up Your Local Agentic System on Nov 20, or have Claude Code installed and working on your computer. Codex also works, but Claude Code is preferred.

title: Distribution Without the Copy-Paste
summary: Prepare every platform's caption, alt text and metadata at once, and still post each item yourself.
description: A finished post still has to go out to four platforms, each with its own caption length, hashtags, alt text and, for YouTube, a title, description and tags. This session shows how to prepare all of it in one step. Live: /wf-pack builds a review-ready folder per platform, and /desk is where a person reviews and posts by hand. Scheduling is available, but it always asks first. The tools prepare. Your team posts. Presented by James Christopher.
agenda: 1. What every platform needs: caption length, hashtags, alt text and YouTube metadata
2. Live: /wf-pack builds a review-ready folder per platform
3. Live: review and post by hand from /desk
4. Scheduling, and why it always asks first
takeaways: A weekly distribution routine for a small team
prerequisites: Attend Set Up Your Local Agentic System on Nov 20, or have Claude Code installed and working on your computer. Codex also works, but Claude Code is preferred.

title: Keeping It Yours: Light Quality Checks for a Small Team
summary: Keep your voice and your facts intact as production speeds up, without adding an approval committee.
description: Once production speeds up, the voice can slip and claims can go out unchecked. This session shows a few quick checks that hold every draft to your own standards. Live: /audit scores a draft for AI tells and sends it back to a person after two failed revisions. /human repairs stiff copy, /fact verifies claims with sources, and /hook compares first lines. Presented by James Christopher.
agenda: 1. Where voice slips and claims go unchecked as production speeds up
2. Live: /audit scores a draft for AI tells
3. Live: /human repairs stiff copy, /fact verifies claims with sources, and /hook compares first lines
4. Start your taste charter
takeaways: A taste charter template
The Zero-Clickbait, Zero-Robot Guide
The four rules as a team policy
prerequisites: Attend Set Up Your Local Agentic System on Nov 20, or have Claude Code installed and working on your computer. Codex also works, but Claude Code is preferred.

description: Our Q1 2027 cohort, AI for Business Executives, starts the week of January 11. It is a live, guided program for leaders who do not code but want AI to take real work off their plate. Each week has one 90-minute live session: a short lesson, a live demo, then hands-on practice with help in the room. Weekly office hours give you time to bring questions and anything that did not work. Early sessions cover getting set up, building a meeting and note-taker workflow, and an accounting workflow. Later sessions move into assistants and agents built for your own role. Seats are limited to 30. Join the interest list to save your spot and get the full curriculum when it is released.
agenda: Welcome and how the cohort works
What AI agents are and what they can do for an executive
Getting set up: accounts and connecting email, calendar and files
Live demo: an assistant working on real tasks
Hands-on: set up your own workspace with help
Wrap-up and first homework
takeaways: A working AI setup connected to your email, calendar and files
A clear picture of what you will build over the cohort
Your first small task automated
A plan for which work to hand to AI first

title: Q1 Cohort: Office Hours
summary: Weekly drop-in help for Q1 cohort members: bring your questions and whatever didn't work this week.
description: A live, open session every Friday during the Q1 cohort, led by Greg and James. Bring your questions from Monday's class, the build step you got stuck on, or a real task you want your agent to handle. We work through it together on screen, so everyone learns from each other's questions. Drop in for as long as you need. Office hours also continue for 30 days after the last class.
agenda: Quick round: what everyone is working on this week
Questions sent in ahead of time
Live help on your own files and agents
Open floor for anything else
takeaways: Answers to what got you stuck this week
Your build step finished, or a clear next step
Ideas from how others in the cohort are using their agents
prerequisites: Have Claude open and the file or task you want help with ready. If you can, send your question ahead of time so we can group similar ones

title: Set Up Your Local Agentic System
summary: Install Claude Code and the agent plugin on your own computer, check each step, and run your first workflow. No coding needed.
description: Setup comes first, so this session does it with you. You install Claude Code and load the jchrisa-agents plugin. You check every step on your own computer. Then you run one complete workflow from start to finish on synthetic data. Every step is a pasted command. You see what scout, fixer and builder each do. You write a task with a done-when check, then run a writing check on a short paragraph. Live: /wf-council, which stress-tests a plan from five angles. Presented by James Christopher.
agenda: 1. Install and check
2. /wf-council first run
3. Agents and skills in plain terms
4. plan.md with a done-when check
5. Writing gate with ai-tell-auditor and humanize-text
6. Questions and take-home
takeaways: Claude Code, the agent plugin and the supporting files installed and checked on your machine, with a pass or fail box for every install step
Your first /wf-council run, saved in ~/Documents/council/runs/
prerequisites: A Claude subscription or Claude Code access, and a computer where you can open a terminal. No coding experience needed.

title: Write Your First Skill File
summary: Read what is inside an agent file and a skill file, then write one skill for a job your team repeats every week.
description: Open the agent and skill files from the setup session and read them part by part. The description field says when the lead agent calls an agent. The model choice sets cost and speed, and the tool limits set what the agent may read or change. You make one edit to an agent file and see the result. Then pick a job your team repeats every week, write one skill for it and test it on synthetic data. You leave with one working skill saved on your computer. Presented by James Christopher.
agenda: 1. Recap of what the setup installed and where the files live
2. Anatomy of an agent file
3. Anatomy of a skill file
4. Pick the weekly job and write the skill
5. Test on synthetic data
6. Questions and take-home
takeaways: Each part of an agent file explained in your own words, with one edit made
One skill written for a weekly team job, tested on synthetic data and saved
prerequisites: Attend Set Up Your Local Agentic System on Nov 20, or have Claude Code installed and working on your computer. Codex also works, but Claude Code is preferred.
